TerraLab’s [AI Agent plugin][plugin] for QGIS brings natural language automation 
to open-source GIS workflows. I tested it and found that it is a valuable 
addition to QGIS's functionality. It is one of the few AI agent QGIS plugins 
that worked for me; with many others, I either had problems installing them or 
encountered payment issues for the paid plan. While the Python plugin is 
[open-source][repo] (under the GPL), it relies on a proprietary backend service 
whose free tier is limited to five tasks per month. The next paid plan costs 49 
CHF per month and can be cancelled at any time. The backend seems to be more 
data-protection-friendly than usual, however: It sends metadata rather than full 
geometries along with the query.

The plugin can drive a large range of GIS capabilities:

* 700+ datasets and 55+ connectors: The plugin offers data access via 
OpenStreetMap, STAC, WMS/WFS/XYZ, and open-data portals
* 300+ processing tools: The plugin can use core open-source processing 
functionality including native QGIS algorithms, GDAL, GRASS, and SAGA
* Database handling and layer editing: The plugin handles database field 
modifications, joins, and SQL queries directly across project layers as well as 
PostGIS, GeoPackage, and SpatiaLite databases
* Plugin and workflow automation: The plugin generates Python code, compiles 
processing steps into reusable QGIS Processing Models, and can control 39 
third-party plugins (for example, QuickMapServices, ORS Tools, DataPlotly, and 
qgis2web).

Additional data sources can enter processing directly via the chat upload or by 
specifying URLs when prompted by the plugin. Styling of the data display works 
by parameterising standard QGIS renderers and labels, but seems not to support 
custom point symbol libraries, at the time of writing.

The [TerraLab website][website] has more information (text in German, short demo 
video in English). And Hans van der Kwast has posted a [review video][video].

Give it a spin, if you like. I would be interested to hear your insights and 
opinions on either Mastodon or LinkedIn.
